title: RSOS and SRC-X.5: every sealed claim, with its number, baseline and caveat
summary: One shared decision selector (the seed) and the RSOS operator language, tested on real tools, real data and real models against each domain's standard method and against plain rollout; every test pre-registered and sealed before it ran; failures kept. Strongest results: CONF6 (AI-AI system: accuracy 1.000 vs 0.875 with 51 % fewer tokens vs plain rollout), CONF5 (AI agents: accuracy 0.95 vs 0.83 with 43 % fewer tokens vs plain rollout), CONF1 (beats the standard in four domains at Holm p < 1e-5), blind planning (318/320 exact; 48/48 on beacon-drawn tasks).
what_is_new: The individual mechanisms (rollout, plan-then-execute, early-stopping self-consistency, scenario MPC, context compression) exist. What is new is one operator language bound unchanged across unrelated hosts (AI agents, AI-AI and AI-human communication, inventory, satellite downlink, energy, robotics), each tested sealed against that host's standard method and against plain rollout, with every claim, including failures, in an open, hash-verified record (SRC-X.5).
not_claimed: results outside the sealed cells (production transfer not yet tested)

claims.claim: Binding a whole two-model AI-AI system to one RSOS structure beats plain rollout on accuracy and tokens
claims.result: accuracy 1.000 vs 0.875 (25 better, 0 worse; Holm p 1.3e-7); tokens 1,286 vs 2,645 (-51 %, 180/200 cells, p 5.1e-28)
claims.caveat: the test does not separate its two parts (binding B; the completeness check)

claims.claim: The RSOS structure identified per host beats plain rollout
claims.result: 7.3k vs 12.9k tokens (-43 %), accuracy 0.95 vs 0.83, Holm p 1.9e-13, 44/48 cells
claims.criteria: met (row 1 of 3; CONF5 met in 2 of 3 rows)

claims.claim: Same, satellite downlink on real orbits
The full seed beats each domain's standard method in all four domains at Holm p < 1e-5
claims.result: AI agents 58-69 % fewer tokens, accuracy +0.11/+0.15 (p 8e-11, 5e-27); AI-human 42 % fewer tokens (5e-21); inventory +1.42 %, 12/12 (1e-9); satellite +1.67 %, 12/12 (1e-9), +1.33 % over the look-ahead MILP
claims.baseline: each domain's standard method (ReAct / self-consistency; direct reply; base-stock; value-per-MB queue)

claims.claim: Communication principle: fewer tokens at equal or better results
claims.result: AI agents 48-61 % fewer tokens (p 8e-9, 2e-21); AI-human 42 % (8e-25); AI-AI 25 % on 150 cells (1e-9)

claims.claim: Operator chains written by a fresh agent from the RSOS sources beat the standard
claims.result: AI agents (self-consistency) 45 % fewer tokens (2e-23); AI-AI 27 % (8e-12); satellite +1.01 %, 22/23 (1e-7); AI-human not passed
claims.caveat: a control agent without the RSOS sources has not been run
plan caches were not cleared between jobs; consistent with leakage, not proven; intervals assume an independence that did not fully hold

claims.claim: Seed beats the standard in seven of ten domains under the pre-registered rule
claims.result: shown in AI agents, AI-AI, AI-human, inventory (+1.36 %, 8/8), energy (+5.79 %, 12/16), satellite (+1.50 %, 8/8), robotics (14.3 % less control effort); four after Holm correction across units
claims.criteria: shown in 7 of 10; not shown: quantum measurement, neural sensing; classification undecided

claims.claim: Does the general structure alone (domain-written levers off) beat plain rollout?
claims.caveat: the gains come from the domain-written levers

claims.claim: Do programs written by an AI given the RSOS sources beat programs by the same AI without them?
claims.result: AI agents (ReAct) 6.7k vs 12.0k tokens (-44 %), accuracy 0.93 vs 0.91, Holm p 4.9e-16, 39/40; other rows no difference
claims.baseline: same AI without the RSOS sources (same compiled operator channels in both arms)

claims.claim: Does switching off one operator cost the gain?
claims.result: full RSOS beat the standard in every row (p 1e-25, 3e-16, 2e-15), but the operators switched off were barely chosen
claims.baseline: full RSOS with one operator off
claims.criteria: not met (0 of 3); design error disclosed

claims.claim: Blind planning: the model names keys, a runtime computes values
claims.result: 318 of 320 pre-registered tasks exact across six models from four companies, at 0.45-0.61x the cost per correct task; the 2 failures were refused by the runtime, none silent

claims.claim: Against the strongest rival patterns, tasks drawn from a public randomness beacon after predictions were public
claims.result: blind planning 48/48 exact; Python that sees the state 48/48; blind Python 47/48; one-call JSON Patch 46/48 (bad steps in the last quarter); tool-calling agent 15/16 at about 100 calls per task
claims.caveat: not more compact than plain Python

claims.claim: Failures follow the number of independent error windows an operation spans
claims.result: one-call JSON Patch per-step error 0.19 % (first quarter of a plan) to 2.33 % (last), Mantel-Haenszel OR 12.3 (95 % CI 6.1-24.7); blind planning flat; SQLite failure 30.7 % to 72.0 % across lock cycles
claims.criteria: met; 26 of 76 agent predictions failed and are reported

claims.result: all seven criteria met: six carriers byte-identical (incl. delay-tolerant link with 30 % loss); failover with 2 of 3 mirrors down; interfaces conform; MCP agent verify/reject; 600/600 invalid quarantined, 0/200 valid blocked; 400 hostile requests, no failure; head time-stamped on Bitcoin

claims.claim: SRC-X.5 v1.5: MCP over HTTP, A2A, install, convergence across nodes, submission by issue
claims.result: 8 of 8 local tests met (one after a disclosed fix); deployment checks 3 of 4 met, IPFS id met only in an alternative form
